literal: Knowledge those-without, they themselves themselves which-afflict suffering, to-enemies-even doing is-difficult.
translation: The suffering that the ignorant inflict upon themselves is hard even for their enemies to cause.
modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் தங்களுக்குத் தாங்களே உண்டாக்கிக் கொள்ளும் துன்பத்தை, அவர்களுடைய பகைவர்களாலும் அவர்களுக்குச் செய்வது கடினம்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the self-destructive nature of ignorance. The phrase 'அறிவு இலார்' refers to those lacking wisdom or proper understanding. Because of their foolish actions, they bring 'பீழை' (suffering) upon themselves. The poet emphasizes the severity of this self-inflicted harm by stating that even their worst enemies ('செறுவார்க்கும்') would find it difficult to cause them such immense pain. Thus, ignorance is portrayed as a person's greatest enemy.
